chunks: Where to place termination components. The question: If external termination components are used, where should they be placed? On the source, sink, or somewhere in between?
A termination resistor stops a signal from bouncing back along a line. Where you put it matters as much as its value.
A series resistor goes at the source, right at the driver pin. A parallel resistor goes at the far end, at or just past the last receiver. Never in the middle.
Any trace between the resistor and the point it serves is a stub that reflects on its own.
Think of a shout down a long corridor. A pillow held at the far wall soaks up the sound, so nothing echoes back. That is parallel termination.
Or you can talk softly and keep a pillow right behind you: the echo comes back once and dies in that pillow at your end. That is series termination.
A pillow halfway down the corridor just blocks the sound and leaves the far wall bare.
The resistor sits at the driver output. Together with R out it makes up Z 0 .
The short piece between the driver pin and the resistor is the only unterminated stub; keep it a few millimetres.
Series termination: a resistor at the driver so the driver plus resistor equals the line impedance ("Series vs parallel termination tradeoffs").
Parallel (end) termination: a resistor about equal to Z 0 at the far end that absorbs the wave ("Source vs sink termination and matching").
Stub: any trace between the net and its resistor or receiver. It reflects if too long. Daisy chain: a bus where one line passes each receiver in turn.
Rise time ( t r ): the edge speed. It sets how short stubs must be.
A driver has 20 ohms output impedance and drives a 50 ohms line. The series resistor is R s equals 50 minus 20 equals 30 ohms, placed at the driver pin. A 3.
3 volts driver then launches half the voltage, 1. 65 volts. At an open far end the wave doubles to 3. 3 volts.
The reflection returns and is absorbed by the matched source, so there is no ringing. That is the whole idea.
"Series termination goes at the source, right next to the driver pin, so that driver plus resistor equals Z0 and absorbs the reflection coming back.
Parallel termination goes at the far end, at or just past the last receiver, so it absorbs the wave on arrival.
In both cases the stub to the resistor must be short compared with the edge.
Never in the middle: a mid-line series resistor splits the line into mismatched pieces, and a mid-line shunt resistor reflects and leaves the end unterminated."
